summary.text: William Tong is Connecticut's Democratic Attorney General, in office since 2019 and the party's nominee for re-election. A litigator and longtime state representative, he was elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022; CT Mirror reports he has filed or joined more than 40 lawsuits challenging federal policies since Donald Trump returned to office.

paragraphs.text: Tong grew up in the Hartford area and graduated from Phillips Academy Andover, Brown University and the University of Chicago Law School.
Tong practiced for 18 years as a litigator, at Simpson Thacher & Bartlett in New York and at Finn Dixon & Herling in Stamford.
He then served six terms, or 12 years, as a state representative, including as House chairman of the Judiciary Committee, and is the first Asian American elected to state office in Connecticut.
Tong was elected Attorney General in 2018, took office in 2019 and was re-elected in 2022.
